title: High-sigma S=4 Figure 1 stress-extension surfaces
purpose: Production-scale extension beyond sigma_env=2.0 to locate where mixed-slope buffering bends, saturates, or enters a high-variability stress regime.
rationale: The first high-resolution S=4 production surface shows positive aligned slopes changing strongly above sigma_env=1.0, while mixed slopes remain comparatively buffered through sigma_env=2.0.

Extending to sigma_env=3.0 and 4.0 is ecologically plausible as a high-variability or boom-bust regime for taxa such as many invertebrates, but should be labelled as a stress extension rather than a universal community baseline.
The extension starts above the previous production grid to avoid recomputing already validated sigma_env values.
The same rho_env grid, replicate count, shard size, and execution defaults are retained so the extension can be merged or compared cleanly with fig1-s4-highres-v1 summaries.
acceptance_checks: The combined parquet validates against the production manifest.
Rows equal 180000, with 1000 replicates for every scenario.
rho_eff and rho_clipped are present and manifest-consistent.
Floor/extinction frequency is summarised before any high-sigma panel is used in main-text inference.
High-sigma results are compared with fig1-s4-highres-v1 before deciding whether to extend the main Figure 1 axis, use an inset, or move the stress region to supplementary material.
